text.p: Following is a factfile on Eric
Cantona, who on Sunday announced his retirement from
professional soccer:
1966: Born May 24 in Paris.
1983: Makes professional debut for Auxerre.
1987: Fined for punching his own goalkeeper. Makes his debut
for France against West Germany.
1988: Joins Marseille. Banned from France side for a year
for swearing at coach Henri Michel.
1989: Suspended indefinitely by Marseille after kicking the
ball into the crowd and throwing shirt at a referee. Moves to
Montpellier.
1990: Banned for 10 days after assaulting team mate
Jean-Claude Lemoult. Returns to Marseille.
1991: Joins Nimes. Banned for throwing the ball at a
referee. At the resulting disciplinary hearing he screams the
word "Idiot" in the face of every committee member. His
suspension is doubled. Cantona responds by announcing his
retirement.
1992: Resurfaces in England. Joins Leeds for 900,000 pounds
($1.5 million). Helps them win the championship before suddenly
moving to rivals Manchester United for 1.2 million pounds ($2
million).
1993: Sent off in United's European Cup defeat by Turkey's
Galatasaray in Istanbul. Scuffles with Turkish police. Banned
for four European matches.
1994: Sent off twice in four days but insists "my love
affair with English soccer is not over". Scores twice in F.A.
Cup final as United complete double. Arrested after a dust-up
with an official before a World Cup semifinal in the United
States.
1995: After being sent off at Crystal Palace in January,
launches a flying "kung-fu" style kick at an abusive fan. Banned
from soccer for eight months. Given a two-week prison sentence,
later reduced on appeal to 120 hours community service. Scores
against Liverpool in first game back.
1996: His finest season. Voted Footballer of the Year and
scores winning goal in F.A. Cup final against Liverpool as
United complete another double.
1997: Wins fifth English championship title in six years.
